key_insight: Morphology plays a crucial role in determining the performance and stability of organic solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing these morphological parameters can lead to the development of high-performing and durable organic solar cells.
method: Calculates current-voltage (JV) curves for complex heterojunction morphologies with low computation time.
Uses morphology-aware descriptors for light absorption, exciton dissociation, and carrier mobilities.
Validated against Monte Carlo and 3D drift-diffusion simulations.
evidence_signal: The method was applied to P3HT:PCBM and PM6:Y6 systems, highlighting the physical trade-offs in performance optimization.
watch_item: The relationship between morphology and performance is material-dependent, which may limit the generalizability of findings.
paper_title: Predicting Organic Solar Cell Performance and Stability from Fast, Morphology-aware Current-Voltage Modeling
